description: Reviewed DX interface: field documentation and complete examples; PHP array inputs and presence/fallback helpers. Historical migration hashes remain in the predecessor file. The library fixture now uses default positional requests; payment and Flint retain explicit object-style coverage. Automatic named sharing replaces repeated inline types with equivalent named references, ExactNumber is exported automatically, and the library fixture exercises default payload returns with WithResponse companions. Existing payment and Flint profiles explicitly retain Result returns. Retry budgets narrow TypeScript idempotency options per operation and remove forced single-attempt examples; mutation examples use persisted key variables. PHP resource signatures are unchanged. Client setup now wraps runtime options in a package-specific ClientOptions alias so baseUrl is optional only with a declared server. These four fixtures declare no server and still require baseUrl; their PHP resource signatures are unchanged. Modular output hashes the sorted declaration modules and resource interfaces. Consumer typechecks retain the existing API; PHP reflection explicitly autoloads generated classes and retains the previous public-signature hashes. Identical nongeneric type expressions now share declarations through aliases, retaining symbol and field documentation. Selective declarations now re-export the same runtime helpers and supporting types as their JavaScript entry points; root declarations are unchanged by this correction. Webhook verification accepts Node/Express and Fetch headers, one secret or readonly rotation arrays, and shared known-envelope aliases with event-name literals. PHP verifier arguments use guarded mixed boundaries with documented string/header-map/secret types so invalid inputs produce SDK errors; unrelated public signatures remain unchanged. Value semantics 4 removes implicit shaped-object index signatures and makes unknown object variants opaque. Ordinary number/float/double fields use native numbers; decimal/int64/uint64 retain exact strings. Date-time inputs accept globalThis.Date or DateTimeInterface; responses retain strings. Independent generated-client and consumer compilation cases cover these changes. Typed PHP responses now have reusable nested entities, array dictionaries, normalized accessors, and event-key-based webhook classes. PHPStan and independent runtime cases verify these intentional breaking PHP changes; Node interface hashes are unchanged. Numeric field documentation now follows the codec representation: plain number/float/double comments no longer request exact strings. The refreshed Node hashes contain only JSDoc changes; declarations without comments and executable source remain unchanged. Simple nullable response wrappers now retain their known object types and typed PHP entities; true polymorphic variants remain opaque. The combined hashes include the numeric JSDoc correction and this reviewed nullable representation correction. Generated examples now place declared idempotency keys in request options and omit unused trailing params when no options follow. Only the Node JSDoc example hashes change; declarations without comments and both target implementations remain identical. Response declarations preserve source component names and public shapes while codecs remain shared. Credential headers supplied by an operation's permitted authentication modes and configured API-version pins are omitted from method inputs; anonymous operations and operations whose modes never supply a declared header retain that input field; the small Flint and risk fixtures remove only the version fields and PHP version getters. Existing exports, ordinary headers, idempotency inputs and PHP response class identities are retained. Dedicated synthetic TypeScript inference, PHPStan, runtime and saved-contract migration tests verify the new behavior, including wire validation for scalar/array credential headers and unchanged anonymous/bearer-only header inputs and compatibility expectations. The four fixture declaration hashes are unchanged by these review corrections. Node now exports VerifiedWebhook, KnownWebhookEvent and per-event WebhookEvent<EventName> types with PHP naming parity. The verifier has an equivalent named return shape, and unchanged allOf envelope models share declaration references. Independent strict TypeScript consumers verify names, exhaustiveness and unknown-event handling before refreshing only payment and Flint Node hashes; executable Node modules/descriptors, PHP output and existing root exports retain their prior baselines. SDK error subclass namespace exports now appear at the Node root and resource subpaths, and declared webhooks add a standalone verifier plus unknown-event/unmatched-envelope reasons. These additive declarations are verified by independent strict TypeScript, PHPStan and injected-transport class matrices. The PHP signature inventory now includes each Errors sub-namespace class and its SdkError parent; existing constructor/method signatures remain unchanged. PHP standalone Webhooks::verify is now included for declared verification, with four mixed parameters preserving SDK validation guards. Client and standalone methods delegate to the shared compiled verifier and retain class identity, recognition reasons and client redaction. Collision consumers independently verify unchanged ValidationError, ApiError and Errors model names alongside the error namespaces. Credential providers now widen every Node credential position to string | CredentialProvider and export that type from roots and resource subpaths. PHP adds Credential and CredentialProvider with redacted credential inspection and widens token/shortcut constructors. Shared per-attempt, validation, invalidation, idempotency and generated-consumer typechecks independently verify this additive interface change. Runtime safety intentionally widens webhook byte bodies to Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer in Node and adds the PHP Errors\TimeoutError class. Existing operation input/output shapes and exports are retained. Independent webhook-byte, timeout-class and generated-consumer regression tests verify these interface additions before refreshing declaration/signature hashes.
